raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Fix LTX-2.3 eager regressions without globally removing the fused head-gate or RMSNorm/modulation kernels.

Image-conditioned stage 1 splits guidance into batch-1 forwards. Video retains per-token timesteps, but audio uses per-sample AdaLN and enters RMSNorm modulation fusion. GPU-only timings do not characterize this host-bound path.

The initial version of this PR addressed launch overhead but did not establish recovery against the original good revision. Further same-machine interleaved comparisons identified redundant AdaLN layout work and a separate Blackwell stage-2 sharding regression. Companion #47301 handles shared Blackwell attention routing; this PR alone is not the complete Blackwell fix.

## Changes

- Reuse `replay_launches` for head-gate and RMSNorm modulation, caching launch metadata rather than tensors or outputs. Keep both fused kernels.
- Move head-gate eligibility/fallback inside the cached operator instead of repeating it in the model.
- Avoid the value-major allocation for singleton AdaLN rows, which are already contiguous. Preserve per-token layout where the broadcast-only fused consumers cannot apply; retain contiguous batched broadcast rows.
- Use automatic stage-2 CFG-rank Ulysses on Hopper and on Blackwell with BCG enabled. Blackwell eager does not amortize the extra dispatch; disabling it for graph mode as well would lose an existing benefit. Preserve explicit sequence parallelism and the existing token threshold.
- Extend launch-cache, fallback, fresh-input, graph, compile, AdaLN-layout and CFG/SP topology tests. Document existing image-conditioned BCG warmup and automatic stage-2 platform selection.

No new knobs, kernel arithmetic changes, quality-tier changes, GT updates, or performance-baseline changes. Existing production-file churn: +35/-12 across four files; no new production files. Tests/docs: +174/-14.

## Validation and Provenance

Original good: `02b983603d34c6af09e554ed2b8bf8d85290d9ae`. Current base: `58214f648c812c70bfd57f0b4196de494f75c0bc`.

Same task-owned H200/B300 machines and dependencies, public `Lightricks/LTX-2.3`, 768x512x121, seed 42, official two-stage schedule, CFG2, TP/SP1, `quality=lossless`, compile disabled, explicit `--ltx2-two-stage-device-mode original`; DiT resident, text/image encoder and VAE layerwise offloaded. Stage timing synchronization is enabled identically. No profiler requests are used for performance medians. Each process has one warmup followed by changing-input measured requests.

Initial measured runtime candidate: `7ad0ae895ae701894dd68fc906362a51ff9a6c54`. Final combined head `02dc569408cd24bd6fee91086c93829cd076b1ef` includes model head `698a5afb05c3e9f0738df4a59b66acc5847d4360` and attention head `115643e05b80622fc0a887dc8a8dbec570cde35e`. It preserves Blackwell stage-2 sharding in graph mode and exact-quality attention routing. Each run records its SHA; intermediate results are distinguished below.

H200, five measured requests per run:

| Workload | Original good stage 1 / stage 2 | Fixed stage 1 / stage 2 | Fixed client E2E |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TI2V eager | 8.649-8.882 / 1.416-1.420 s | 8.665 / 0.962 s | 10.950 s |
| T2V eager | Not rerun on original good | 5.368 / 0.948 s | 7.604 s |
| TI2V, matching-image BCG warmup | Not rerun on original good | 6.100 / 0.844 s | 8.322 s |
| T2V BCG | Not rerun on original good | 5.288 / 0.805 s | 7.408 s |

The last three configurations are neutral against the initial #47270 head. Ranges are independent-run medians, not confidence intervals. H200 behavior does not depend on the companion Blackwell attention patch.

B300, 9-request good/fixed/good comparison: stage 1 **9.262 / 9.039 / 9.382 s**, stage 2 **0.767 / 0.749 / 0.767 s**, client E2E **11.355 / 11.148 / 11.446 s**. The fixed run uses the combined candidate `7ad0ae895ae701894dd68fc906362a51ff9a6c54`. Earlier smaller runs varied; the interleaved comparison supports recovery, not a hardware-independent extra percentage gain. Disabling both fused paths did not recover the original performance; attention routing and stage-2 communication mattered independently.

The execution mode matters for stage 2 too: B300 T2V BCG takes approximately 0.465 s with CFG-rank sharding versus 0.671 s without it. The final patch preserves this graph-mode benefit while avoiding the roughly 0.3 s loss in eager. Final combined head `02dc569408cd24bd6fee91086c93829cd076b1ef` passed both graph configurations with five changing-input requests each:

| B300 workload | Stage 1 | Stage 2 | Client E2E |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| TI2V, matching-image BCG warmup | 3.374 s | 0.487 s | 5.073 s |
| T2V BCG | 2.742 s | 0.467 s | 4.469 s |

The same final combined head was rerun for nine eager requests: stage 1 **9.161 s**, stage 2 **0.753 s**, client E2E **11.251 s**. This remains within the matched original-good range.

Accuracy scope:

- Focused operator tests cover fresh tensors, JIT-dispatch avoidance for warmed signatures, real graphs, Inductor, and CPU/strided/broadcast fallbacks.
- AdaLN tests preserve values exactly while checking the required layouts and avoiding redundant allocation.
- H200: five final-layout videos match the preceding candidate pixel-for-pixel; those five also match the original public PR head. Audio is not universally bit-identical (final-layout comparison MSE 0 to 4.52e-7); unchanged baselines also vary. No GT was changed.
- B300: switching attention backends and stage-2 reduction topology is not bit-exact. Against the initial PR head, five matched videos have full-video PSNR 25.63-31.31 dB and audio MSE 0.000328-0.008539. These are observed differences, not a quality pass or proof of closer agreement with the official reference. Fresh-input operator tests compare captured FA4 against cuDNN with the existing BF16 tolerance; full server consistency results are reported separately.
- These isolated comparisons do not establish bitwise equivalence against every intervening optimization since original-good, nor do H200/B300 establish recovery of all historical H100 cross-runner timing differences.

An additional B300 `exact` TI2V check isolates the model patch from attention routing: model-only head `698a5afb05c3e9f0738df4a59b66acc5847d4360` produces the same decoded video SHA256 as the preceding `61bb5547b67db0aebbcba15017e5e6921a56e9c6` (`2743239da33f0fdbd15c140fa33df165a52cb3c50f5b38b193ea39bae5c21482`). An ungated companion attention candidate changed this output and failed the existing official-reference CLIP threshold; it was fixed before publication. Final combined head `02dc569408cd24bd6fee91086c93829cd076b1ef` matches all 25 video frames and decoded audio samples bit-for-bit. Existing pinned official GT (`c7258eb56e9951878c66fc0fb3673d9f4775b0b2`) passes unchanged thresholds: CLIP 0.5749, SSIM 0.3431, PSNR 12.0377, max MAD 43.2833.

Standard-server limitation: B300's `b200.json` has no LTX performance baseline, and existing official TI2V images lack a `case_map.json` entry. The direct pinned-image comparison above uses existing metrics and thresholds but does not turn the standard server test into a pass.

Pre-commit passed. H200 focused tests passed at model head `15e7a2c8d8eedd2325b3d6613b61963060d794b1`; the subsequent model change only restores the Blackwell graph-mode branch. Final combined head `02dc569408cd24bd6fee91086c93829cd076b1ef` passed the full focused suite on B300, including real CFG/SP folding and registered graph routing. Additional shared-context/CFG/LoRA/cache/model coverage: 69 passed, 4 subtests. Exact CI status is reported separately; pending CI is not treated as passed.

@@ -93,9 +93,13 @@ For latency-oriented LTX serving, prefer CFG parallel over sequence parallelism.
 
 Use `--enable-cfg-parallel` for degree-2 CFG parallel. Use `--cfg-parallel-size` only when you explicitly need a different CFG branch count. If `resident` exceeds available VRAM, keep the same parallelism preset and switch only the device mode to `original`.
 
+On Hopper GPUs, and on Blackwell when breakable CUDA graphs are enabled, sufficiently long stage-2 sequences automatically reuse the CFG ranks for Ulysses. Other configurations keep stage 2 unsharded unless you explicitly configure sequence parallelism.
+
 On high-VRAM GPUs, add `--text-encoder-cpu-offload false` if text encoding latency matters and you have enough memory.
 
-On GPUs with at least 130 GiB (H200, B200, B300), `LTX2TwoStagePipeline` serving turns on breakable CUDA graphs by default when the DiTs stay resident (LTX-2.3: `resident` mode). Warmup captures the default 768x512, 121-frame request; other resolutions or frame counts run eager, so pass `--warmup-resolutions` and `--warmup-num-frames` for the shape you serve (the OpenAI video API defaults to 4 seconds, which LTX rounds to 89 frames). Pass `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph false` to run eager.
+On GPUs with at least 130 GiB (H200, B200, B300), `LTX2TwoStagePipeline` serving turns on breakable CUDA graphs by default when the DiTs stay resident (LTX-2.3: `resident` mode). Warmup captures the default 768x512, 121-frame **text-to-video** request; other resolutions or frame counts run eager, so pass `--warmup-resolutions` and `--warmup-num-frames` for the shape you serve (the OpenAI video API defaults to 4 seconds, which LTX rounds to 89 frames). Pass `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph false` to run eager.
+
+For image-conditioned serving, also add `--warmup-sampling-params '{"image_path":["/path/to/reference.png"]}'` to the server command. Use a reference image accessible to the server and the same conditioning layout as your requests. Matching resolution and frame count alone is insufficient: TI2V uses different guidance batches and timestep shapes from T2V. Requests that do not match the captured conditioning signature still run eager.
